en.title: Faker Tapped to Lead South Korea's Fight Against Online Gambling Epidemic
en.summary: Gaming icon Faker is stepping into a new role, joining forces with the South Korean government to combat a surge in youth online gambling. His mission: to leverage his global recognition and personal values to guide young people away from addiction.
en.body:
In a significant move that bridges the gap between esports stardom and public welfare, **Lee Sang-hyeok**, the legendary **League of Legends** player known globally as **Faker**, has been appointed an honorary Senior Officer in the South Korean police force. His new mandate is to spearhead the nation's campaign against a growing online gambling epidemic, particularly among its youth. This initiative comes as online betting platforms see explosive growth worldwide, prompting a global wave of regulatory scrutiny and crackdowns, with countries like Cambodia and India restricting operations, and the Philippines and Thailand targeting illegal ventures. The United States, too, is grappling with its own gambling addiction crisis, with experts calling for public health responses and stricter regulation akin to alcohol or tobacco.

South Korea has seen a disturbing rise in illicit online gambling, with young people reportedly going to extreme lengths to fund their habits or cover debts. The government's choice of **Faker** for this crucial role is strategic. As reported by the Seoul Economic Daily, his appointment stems from his status as a globally recognized esports athlete who has consistently embodied values of self-management and restraint throughout his long and illustrious career. This makes him an ideal role model for young individuals facing the allure and dangers of online gambling. In his capacity as an honorary officer, **Faker** will be instrumental in producing public service announcements, including videos and posters, designed to promote South Korea's Youth Cyber Gambling Voluntary Reporting System. This system aims to provide support and resources for youngsters struggling with gambling addiction.

## A Global Concern, A Local Response
The booming global gambling industry, exemplified by massive deals like DraftKings' $350 million partnership with the UFC and the Indian betting app Mobile Premier League achieving unicorn status, stands in stark contrast to the increasing governmental efforts to curb its reach. While some nations are embracing the financial opportunities, others, including South Korea, are prioritizing the protection of their citizens, especially the vulnerable younger demographic. The appointment of **Faker** signifies a proactive, culturally relevant approach to a complex social issue. His influence extends far beyond the esports arena; he is a figure of respect and admiration, making his message against gambling addiction particularly resonant.

## Incentives for Recovery
To further encourage participation in the Youth Cyber Gambling Voluntary Reporting System, the South Korean government is offering a unique incentive: autographed uniforms from **Faker** himself. These prized items will be awarded to young individuals who demonstrate commitment to their recovery by faithfully engaging with treatment programs. This tangible reward serves not only as a token of achievement but also as a symbol of hope and encouragement for their healthy reintegration into daily life. It’s a creative way to leverage the star power of one of gaming's greatest figures to foster positive change and combat a growing societal challenge.

## What's Next
Details regarding the rollout of **Faker**'s public service announcements and the specifics of the reporting system's outreach programs have not yet been fully announced. However, his involvement marks a significant step in South Korea's commitment to addressing online gambling addiction through influential, relatable figures.

tr.title: Faker, Güney Kore'nin Çevrimiçi Kumar Bağımlılığı ile Mücadelesine Liderlik Edecek
tr.summary: Gaming dünyasının efsane ismi Faker, gençleri çevrimiçi kumar bağımlılığından korumak için Güney Kore hükümetiyle işbirliği yapıyor. Faker'ın misyonu, global tanınmışlığını ve kişisel değerlerini gençleri bağımlılıktan uzaklaştırmak için kullanmak.
tr.body:
Faker, **Lee Sang-hyeok**, yani **League of Legends** efsanesi, Güney Kore polisi bünyesinde onursal bir üst düzey subay olarak atandı. Yeni görevi, ülkesindeki gençleri hedef alan çevrimiçi kumar salgınıyla mücadele etmek. Bu girişimle birlikte, dünya genelinde patlama yaşayan çevrimiçi bahis platformlarına karşı düzenleyici denetim ve Operasyonlar artıyor. 
## Küresel Bir Sorun, Yerel Bir Yanıt
Çevrimiçi kumar endüstrisinin büyümesi, DraftKings'in UFC ile 350 milyon dolarlık ortaklığı ve Hint bahis uygulaması Mobile Premier League'in unicorn statüsüne ulaşmasıyla birlikte, hükümetlerin bu sektörün erişimi konusunda endişeleri artıyor. Bazı ülkeler finansal fırsatları değerlendirirken, Güney Kore gibi diğerleri vatandaşlarının, özellikle de gençlerin korunmasına öncelik veriyor. 
Faker'ın ataması, karmaşık bir sosyal sorunla ilgili proaktif ve kültürel olarak ilgili bir yaklaşımı simgeliyor. Etkisi, sadece esports alanıyla sınırlı değil; saygın ve takdir edilen bir figür olarak, kumar bağımlılığına karşı verdiği mesaj özellikle etkili oluyor.
## Kurtulma İçin Teşvikler
Güney Kore hükümeti, Gençlik Siber Kumar Gönüllü Bildirim Sistemi'ne katılımı teşvik etmek için benzersiz bir teşvik sunuyor: Faker'ın imzalı forması. Bu değerli öğeler, tedavi programlarına sadık kalarak iyileşme taahhüdünü gösteren gençlere verilecek. Bu somut ödül, yalnızca bir başarı belgesi değil, aynı zamanda sağlıklı bir şekilde günlük hayata yeniden katılmaları için umut ve cesaret kaynağı olarak hizmet ediyor.
## Sonraki Adımlar
Faker'ın kamu spotlarının ve bildirimin sisteminin tanıtım programlarının detayları henüz tam olarak açıklanmadı. Ancak, onun katılımı, çevrimiçi kumar bağımlılığına karşı etkili, ilgili figürler aracılığıyla mücadele eden Güney Kore'nin taahhüdünün önemli bir adımını temsil ediyor.

content_raw: Online gambling has been in the news a fair bit recently, with the ease of getting into online sportsbook betting becoming a hotly contested issue in the United States and popular prediction markets being subjected to increased controversy and government scrutiny . It's hardly limited to the United States, however, as illicit online gambling has wide appeal across much of Asia, despite local laws forbidding much of it. South Korea in particular has seen an uptick in online gambling, particularly among youth, many of whom have gone to extreme lengths to obtain money to spend on gambling or cover their debts . To help combat the growing problem, the government has teamed up with one of the most famous figures in global esports, League of Legends prodigy Lee Sang-hyeok, better known by the handle "Faker." As reported by the Seoul Economic Daily , Faker has been made an honorary police officer with the title of Senior Officer. The rationale behind this appointment is that "Lee is an esports player with high recognition at home and abroad and has consistently practiced the values of self-management and restraint throughout his long career, serving as a role model for young people." In this role, Lee will be producing public service announcements, such as videos and posters, to help promote South Korea's Youth Cyber Gambling Voluntary Reporting System, which aims to help youngsters with online gambling problems. As an added incentive to free themselves of gambling addiction, those who join the program may receive Faker's autographed uniform, which the article notes "will be delivered to young people who have overcome gambling addiction by faithfully participating in treatment programs, serving as encouragement for their healthy return to daily life." This honor is hardly the first for Lee, who was the first Korean eSports athlete to receive the Cheongnyong Medal , a top honor for the country's athletes. He's also due to appear on South Korean postage and has recently debuted on a local Disney+ television program . Suffice to say, Lee is a broadly known public figure whose high profile might bring attention to the issue. This all contrasts against the actions of League of Legends publisher Riot Games, who opened up sports-betting sponsorships for LoL teams a little over a year ago . Whether or not the South Korean government will actually take them to task for that is up in the air.
